analysis.title: Huang-Over & Hormuz Headlines Hammer Stocks; Spoos Lose As Bonds Snooze
key_insights: Tech/AI derisking drove a broad US equity selloff on Nov 16. NDX fell over 2.5% and every US major index was sold from the open to the close. Only Staples gained, while Tech and Energy were sold.

Nvidia traded back toward last week's lows after reports of Huang's return were reportedly denied by the company's management. The note ties the AI selloff to worries about tightening AI spending and a government block on the China back-door.
NeoClouds were the hardest hit within AI. The Mag7 names underperformed with no safety bid, and SPX ex-AI was also lower.
VIX tested above 24, and the note says the rest of the week is pricing in significant volatility.
Credit weakened again after a few days of reprieve. IG spreads and hyperscaler credit risk widened, and data-center CDS moved back above 450bps.
Oil fell 2-3% (Brent about $93/bbl, WTI about $86/bbl) despite Iran reporting six tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz since Sunday and fresh drone attacks on a US air defense site in Bahrain.

The note attributes the oil decline to a well-supplied physical market. The IEA reported global supply exceeding demand for the first time since the conflict began, and Goldman forecasts a surplus of about 2 million bpd heading into 2027.

A secondary driver of lower oil is market adaptation. Traders and shippers have rerouted around the most dangerous Hormuz corridors, and a third US carrier strike group in the Persian Gulf raises the prospect of a negotiated or military resolution, which is unwinding some tail-risk premium.
Lower crude pulled wholesale diesel down on both sides of the Atlantic. US retail diesel fell below $6 for the first time since September.
Bonds were little changed. The 30Y was unchanged and the belly was down 2-3bps, ahead of a heavy week of Fed speakers.

Fed speakers on Nov 16: Barr warned that autonomous AI agents could accelerate bank runs. Warsh outlined upside (broad productivity gains) and downside (labor market disruption) AI scenarios. Hammack favors smaller, steady rate increases to fight broadening inflation pressure.
December hike odds dipped, removing about 50bps of pricing, while 2027 rate expectations rose. The note calls the short end marginally hawkish.
The dollar extended gains to new 18-month highs. Crypto liquidated over the weekend and erased all post-August 'debasement' trade gains. Gold drifted lower, back below its October lows.

Citing Bloomberg's Frank Monkam, the note says the 'Fed Put' appears to be missing. June 2027 rate expectations rose even as SPX tested the bottom of its recent range, which weakens the case for buying dips.
Record retail buying last week was followed by this drawdown. The note flags tomorrow night's earnings and Anthropic's IPO (likely Thursday) as upcoming events.

tension_points.theme: oil supply glut vs Hormuz risk
tension_points.bull_case: Geopolitical risk premium: Iran reports six tanker strikes in Hormuz since Sunday and fresh drone attacks on a US site in Bahrain.
tension_points.bear_case: The physical market is well-supplied. The IEA says supply exceeded demand for the first time since the conflict began, and Goldman sees a glut of about 2 million bpd in 2027. Gulf exports have largely recovered.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful physical supply shortfall emerging from the Hormuz disruptions would invalidate the glut thesis.

tension_points.theme: dip buying vs missing Fed put
tension_points.bull_case: Retail investors bought heavily last week, and historically equity corrections prompt expectations of a policy backstop through easing.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistent inflation risks complicate easing. June 2027 rate expectations rose even as SPX tested the bottom of its range, so dip alpha is harder to harvest.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Markets repricing toward Fed easing in response to the equity drawdown would invalidate the bear case.
